TasteForge International - Q3 2023 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the TasteForge International Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if you're using a landline, or click the raise hand icon if joining via webcast. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss TasteForge International's Q3 2023 results. Joining me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Growth Officer; and David Ruiz, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2023. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on eight key areas: overall company performance highlights, capital expenditure plans and priorities, updates on M&A activity and portfolio management, discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies, market share trends for major brands, organic revenue growth overall and by region, e-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue, and volume and price/mix analysis.

First, regarding overall company performance highlights: I'm thrilled to kick off with what we believe is our strongest quarter in over a decade, delivering record top- and bottom-line results amid a resilient yet dynamic Food & Beverage landscape. As a leader in beverages, snacks, and ambient foods—with powerhouse brands like our flagship Quench energy drinks, ZestBar protein snacks, and EverFresh dairy alternatives—we've not only met but exceeded our guidance, underscoring the strength of our diversified portfolio and agile execution.

Let me start with the headline numbers. Consolidated net revenues reached $15.4 billion, up 9% on a reported basis and 7% organically year-over-year—outpacing the global F&B category growth of 4.2% per NielsenIQ data. This marks our 11th straight quarter of organic growth, driven by a balanced mix of 2.5% volume expansion, 3.2% net pricing actions, and 1.3% favorable product mix shifts toward higher-margin premium SKUs. Adjusted operating income climbed 14% to $2.6 billion, expanding adjusted operating margins to 17.1%—a 90-basis-point improvement—reflecting our disciplined cost management and supply chain efficiencies. Diluted EPS came in at $1.52, a robust 16% increase and well ahead of consensus estimates of $1.42, while free cash flow surged 22% to $2.1 billion, enabling $1.2 billion in share repurchases and a 12% dividend hike announced today.

Diving deeper into segment performance, our Beverages division—representing 45% of revenues—posted an outstanding 11% organic growth to $6.9 billion. Volume gains were led by functional beverages, where Quench Zero-Sugar surged 18% amid the booming RTD energy category, capturing 2.2 points of market share per IRI scans versus peers like Monster and Red Bull. Premiumization played a key role, with low/no-alcohol and hydration lines like our AquaVita alkaline waters up 25%, aligning with consumer shifts toward health-focused options post-pandemic. Pricing was up 4%, moderated in inflationary hotspots but sustained through targeted promotions.

Snacks & Convenience Foods, at 35% of the mix, grew 8% organically to $5.4 billion, fueled by snacking megatrends. ZestBar's high-protein bars outperformed the $8 billion U.S. nutrition bar category by 300 basis points, thanks to innovative flavors like Matcha Green Tea Protein and expansions into DTC channels via Shopify integrations. Our savory snacks, including kettle chips and plant-based puffs, benefited from +3% volume from new everyday low-price (EDLP) tiers, countering private-label pressures seen at players like PepsiCo's Frito-Lay.

Dairy & Alternatives rounded out at 20%, with $3.1 billion in revenues up 5% organically. Here, EverFresh oat milk and almond yogurts gained traction in the $15 billion plant-based dairy segment, growing 15% versus flat category performance—mirroring Chobani's yogurt dominance but with superior margins from backward-integrated almond sourcing in California. Mix improvements from upsizing to larger multipacks offset softer legacy dairy volumes amid milk price volatility.

Regionally, North America delivered 10% organic growth to $9.2 billion, powered by distribution gains—adding 1,500 ACV points across key retailers like Walmart and Kroger—and e-commerce penetration now at 12% of sales, up from 8% last year. EMEA grew 7% to $3.5 billion, resilient despite Eurozone inflation peaking at 10%, with strong momentum in functional waters in the UK and Germany. APAC accelerated to 12% growth at $1.8 billion, led by India where our affordable sachet packs in mango lassi RTDs captured 4 points of share in the $20 billion traditional beverages market, outpacing local incumbents like Parle Agro. LATAM rounded out at 5% growth to $0.9 billion, navigating FX headwinds but buoyed by volume recovery in Brazil's snack aisles.

Strategically, these results reflect bold technical initiatives we've accelerated. On the supply chain front, our $250 million investment in AI-driven demand sensing—powered by partnerships with IBM Watson—has reduced inventory days by 18% and forecast accuracy to 92%, shielding us from cocoa and sugar commodity spikes that hammered competitors like Hershey earlier this year. Sustainability remains core: we're 25% toward our 2030 net-zero Scope 1&2 goal, with regenerative agriculture on 40% of our nut and fruit supply via precision farming pilots in Vietnam and Mexico. Innovation pipeline is robust, with five NPD launches—including a collagen-infused RTD coffee line targeting the $12 billion functional coffee space—and $400 million earmarked for 2024 capex in high-speed aseptic filling lines to scale plant-based volumes.

Balance sheet-wise, net debt to EBITDA improved to 2.1x from 2.4x, with $4.5 billion in liquidity providing ample firepower for M&A in adjacencies like meal kits or pet nutrition snacks. Consumer trends—health, convenience, and sustainability—are tailwinds, with our household penetration up 1.5 points per Kantar data.

Second, concerning capital expenditure plans and priorities: As we wrap up a strong quarter with adjusted EPS of $1.52, up 16% year-over-year, and organic revenue growth of 7% driven by our core categories in snacks, plant-based proteins, and functional beverages, capex remains a cornerstone of our strategy to drive margin expansion, capture market share in high-growth segments, and build resilience in an increasingly volatile input cost environment.

For FY2024, we're guiding to total capital expenditures of $650 million, a 15% increase from $565 million in FY2023. This represents about 4.2% of our projected net sales of $15.5 billion, which is in line with our peers like PepsiCo and Nestlé, who are also ramping up investments amid softening commodity inflation but persistent labor and energy pressures. We've allocated this capex across four key priorities: capacity expansion (40%, or $260 million), automation and digital transformation (25%, or $162.5 million), sustainability initiatives (20%, or $130 million), and maintenance and supply chain resilience (15%, or $97.5 million).

Capacity expansion is our top priority at $260 million, focusing on high-margin categories where we're gaining share. In plant-based proteins—where we've grown 22% YoY, outpacing the category's 15% CAGR per Nielsen data—we're investing $150 million in a greenfield facility in Vietnam's Binh Duong province. This 250,000-square-foot plant will ramp to 50,000 metric tons of annual capacity by Q4 2025, targeting Asia-Pacific export markets and local demand from partners like Lotte and Tingyi. APAC now represents 28% of our revenue, up from 22% three years ago. Similarly, $80 million for debottlenecking our ready-to-eat meals line in Mexico, adding 20% capacity to serve the $12 billion Latin American convenience food market, and $30 million for a beverage innovation center in India to scale low-sugar functional drinks.

Automation and digital transformation gets $162.5 million to drive our targeted 200 basis points of gross margin expansion over the next two years. Labor costs have risen 10% industry-wide, so we're deploying Industry 4.0 technologies like $75 million rollout of ABB robotics and FANUC systems across five North American plants, boosting throughput by 25% while cutting downtime 15%. $50 million in AI-driven supply chain platforms from SAP and Blue Yonder to optimize our 40,000-SKU portfolio, and $37.5 million for vision systems in Europe for precision filling.

Sustainability initiatives receive $130 million, as ESG drives premium pricing—our sustainable brands grew 30% faster last quarter. $60 million for solar arrays and heat recovery at three US plants, aiming for 25% renewable energy by 2026; $40 million for water stewardship in Brazil; and $30 million for regenerative agriculture pilots scaling to 50,000 acres by 2025.

Maintenance and supply chain resilience at $97.5 million addresses disruptions like Ukraine impacts on sunflower oil. This includes $40 million for cold chain upgrades for e-commerce growth. Regionally, North America gets 45%, Europe 25%, APAC 20%, LatAm 10%. These investments are ROIC-accretive with 18-22% IRR, funded 70% from cash flow.

Third, in terms of updates on M&A activity and portfolio management: As we execute on our Core Growth 2027 strategy, M&A and portfolio management are central to optimizing for sustainable, high-margin growth amid 8-10% YoY commodity inflation, health & wellness shifts, and plant-based demand. We've delivered $450 million in enterprise value from deals over 18 months at 10.2x EBITDA multiples, below the 12.5x industry average per Bain.

Recently completed acquisitions include our $320 million Q2 close of VerdeLeaf Snacks, adding clean-label protein crisps aligned with our wellness platform. Accretive by 75 bps to EPS, with $45 million run-rate synergies: 40% supply chain, 35% SG&A, 25% cross-selling into Kroger and Whole Foods. Early Q3, $180 million for NutriHydra Beverages, expanding functional water TAM by 18% to $28 billion with $65 million FY24 contribution at 28% margins. In APAC, $50 million minority stake in TropiFusion Juices for Southeast Asia premium juices.

On divestitures, Q3 sale of legacy canned soup business for $210 million at 7.8x EBITDA freed $140 million: 60% to VerdeLeaf capex, 30% debt reduction to 2.6x leverage, 10% innovation fund. YTD divestitures $375 million, exiting 12% SKUs to focus Power Brands at 75% revenue, growing 8% organically.

Our playbook pillars: Health & Wellness with AI flavor profiling and regenerative sourcing for 40% snacks; Supply Chain Resilience with IoT and blockchain for EU compliance; Geographic Expansion with $100 million for Europe bolt-ons and APAC e-com. Pipeline $1.2 billion, LOIs on $250 million kombucha and European confectioner. This enhanced EBITDA margins 210 bps to 19.8%.

Fourth, looking at discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies: Our RGM strategies were pivotal in 6.8% organic growth, outpacing industry 4.2% per NielsenIQ, with 4.5% net pricing offsetting 0.3% volume headwind and 2.6% mix in 3.1% commodity inflation.

We executed 17 targeted increases averaging 5.2% on-list, netting 4.5% via SymphonyAI elasticity modeling. Held flat on high-elasticity CSDs vs. private labels. Beverages ASP +5.1%, e.g., 6.8% on AquaVita with -1.2 elasticity. Snacks 4.7%, selective rollbacks; dairy 3.9%, 7.2% on yogurts.

RGM delivered 680 bps value: delisted 14% low-NGP SKUs, shifting to Better-for-You at 35% sales. AI dynamic pricing in 85% NA doors, 14% promo inefficiency cut, reallocating to Fresho Rewards app.

Regionally: NA 5.2% pricing; Europe 3.8% with mix offset; EM 8.4% LatAm, APAC volume-led. Leaning into premiumization, e-com bundles, sustainability premiums. Q4 pricing 4.0-4.5%, margins up 110 bps to 38.2%.

Fifth, reviewing market share trends for major brands: Per IRI 52-week data, total beverage portfolio at 28.7% US dollar share (+120 bps), global 22.4% volume (+80 bps).

AquaFizz CSD at 31.2% (+150 bps), zero-sugar 12% sub-share. VoltEdge energy at 17.5% (+220 bps), Ultra #3 shots. HydraPure sparkling 14.8% (+190 bps), BrewBolt RTD coffee 9.2% (+110 bps).

NA +90 bps to 29.1%; EMEA +140 bps to 19.6%; APAC +200 bps to 18.3%; LATAM flat 24.7%. Pillars: 14 NPDs, 95% ACV convenience, $1.2B marketing at 3.1x ROMI. Expect 100-150 bps gains.

Sixth, analyzing organic revenue growth: overall and by region: Organic growth at 8.2% constant currency, ahead of 6-7% guide. Price 4.1 pts, mix 2.3 pts, volume 1.8 pts.

NA 10.5% (52% revenue), volumes +3.2% Walmart rollout; EMEA 7.1% (24%), aseptic investments; APAC 12.4% (15%), Alibaba alliance; LatAm 4.8% (9%), ERP rollout. Q4 7-9%, targeting 8-10% CAGR.

Seventh, examining e-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue: E-com $185M, +48% YoY, 15.4% of $1.2B revenue (full-year ~13%). DTC 42% (+55%), marketplaces 35% (+42%), quick-com 23% (+62%).

NA $132M (18%); Europe $32M (11%); APAC $21M (9%). AI recommendations +22% conversions, $15M digitization, 42.5% margins. Q4 40% growth to 16.5%, $250M digital capex.

Eighth, considering volume and price/mix analysis: Net sales $15.8B, +10% reported/8% organic: +2% volume, +6% price/mix.

Volumes: Beverages +1% (ZestEnergy +12%); Snacks/Dairy +4%. Regional: NA +1%, EMEA +3%, APAC +5%, LatAm flat. Price/mix: ASP +4.5%, mix +1.5% via AI pricing, SKU rationalization. FY24 $500M innovation.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2023. Net sales were $15.4 billion, representing a 9% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 38.2%, impacted by input cost inflation partially offset by pricing and efficiencies. Operating income was $2.6 billion, and earnings per share were $1.52. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $4.5 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are raising our guidance for organic revenue growth to 8-9%, adjusted EPS to $5.95-$6.05, and operating margins to 16.8%.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Sarah Thompson (CEO):
Thanks, John. Inflation remains a headwind, with commodities like cocoa, sugar, and dairy up 3-10% YoY, but our pricing actions netting 4.5% and supply chain efficiencies—like AI demand sensing reducing inventory days 18%—have more than offset this, expanding margins 90-210 bps. We're hedged on key inputs and focused on premium mix to protect profitability.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Emily Chen (Morgan Stanley):
What are your plans for new product launches and what is the expected impact?

Lisa Patel (Chief Growth Officer):
Great question, Emily. Our innovation pipeline includes collagen-infused RTD coffee targeting $12B functional space, zero-sugar energy shots, and plant-based protein clusters. These 20+ SKUs aim for 15-20% CAGR in health platforms, adding 2-3 points to organic growth via 2.5x category NPS and premium pricing, much like our Quench Zero success gaining 2.2 share points.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

David Lee (JPMorgan):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

David Ruiz (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
David, we're proactive with $250M AI investments via IBM Watson hitting 92% forecast accuracy, robotics boosting throughput 25%, and blockchain for traceability amid Ukraine and El Niño effects. Cold chain upgrades support e-com, and regenerative pilots cut costs 8-10%, keeping us resilient versus peers.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Rachel Gomez with Barclays. Please proceed.

Rachel Gomez (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Michael Chen (CFO):
Rachel, Q4 organic growth 7-9%, with holiday mix tailwinds, e-com at 16.5%, and RGM adding 500-600 bps. Full-year raised to 8-9% organic, EPS $5.95-6.05. We're positioned for 8-10% CAGR, outpacing industry via capex ROIC 18-22% and M&A pipeline.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in TasteForge International. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
